after: The ayah places the male class over women, then names a feared rising by women. Hearing رِجَالٌ as males makes that rising a gendered counter-movement in the same vertical image.
reason: رِجَالٌ can mean male human, while نُشُوزَهُنَّ names women's rising or protrusion. The male class and their rising meet as opposing positions.

after: Both senses evoke human people, though only broadly.
reason: رَجُلٌ as a foot-walker and قَوَّٰمُونَ as a men's collectivity share a human-group image, but the connection is generic.

after: The men can be pictured as walkers alongside سَبِيلًا, the route they may traverse. The role then carries a path image: people moving along a way.
reason: رَجُلٌ in this branch means one who walks on foot; سَبِيلًا is an extended route followed toward a goal. The walker and route complete one another.

after: The men's group can be placed within a human era, but the link is broad.
reason: رَجُلُ فلان can mean his era, while قَوَّٰمُونَ names a men's group. The era supplies only a generic time frame for that group.

after: Both senses point toward existence in time, though the link is broad in the closing clause.
reason: رَجُلُ فلان can mean his time or era, and كَانَ asserts occurrence or presence in time. Their temporal senses overlap.

after: A swarm and a human group share the image of a multitude.
reason: الرَّجْل من الجراد is a large swarm of locusts, while قَوَّٰمُونَ is glossed here as a group of men. Both evoke a collective, but only generically.

after: A watercourse can be followed toward an outlet, as a sought thing is pursued.
reason: رِجْلَة الماء is a watercourse, and تَبْغُوا۟ means seeking or pursuing. The flowing channel can serve as a route toward what is sought, though the link is broad.

after: The way against them can be heard as a channel through the scene. The watercourse and the path give سَبِيلًا a flowing, physical route image.
reason: رِجْلَة الماء is a watercourse, while سَبِيلًا is a route or path. Both are channels through terrain, one carrying water and the other giving passage.

after: The command to strike can be heard beside a bird-foot brand that is itself an applied mark. The pair pictures a blow that leaves an identifying sign.
reason: رَجُلُ الطائر is a kind of branding mark, while وَٱضْرِبُوهُنَّ names striking. Applying a brand by contact makes the strike image a mark-making one.

after: The divine predicate sounds spatially high. Taking the attested upper-tip sense of رِجْلُ القوس, the phrase briefly pictures elevation as the raised end of a bow.
reason: رِجْلُ القوس is glossed as the bow's upper or lower tip, while عَلِيًّا means high or exalted. The upper-tip attestation and عَلِيًّا share a vertical image.

after: The pairing contrasts utterance begun without preparation with ongoing preservation.
reason: الارتجال is speech started without preparation, while حَٰفِظَٰتٌ names guarding or preserving. Spontaneous utterance sits against deliberate keeping, a thin contrast.

after: Together the senses offer a thin image of speech rising suddenly.
reason: الارتجال is speech begun without preparation, while نُشُوزَهُنَّ is rising or protrusion. They can make an image of words erupting upward, though the verse's word names behavior rather than speech.

after: Daylight exposes what the hidden keeps out of sight. The pair makes a movement from concealment toward visibility.
reason: تَرَجَّلَ النهار means the day rises and its light spreads, while الغَيْب is the hidden or unseen. Spreading daylight stands against what remains concealed.

after: The daylight rises, and the feared nushūz is itself a rising. The repeated upward movement gives the two images a shared motion.
reason: تَرَجَّلَ النهار means the day rises, while نُشُوزَهُنَّ means rising or protrusion. Both senses name an upward movement.

after: The closing predicate names highness, echoing the day's ascent. The divine attribute acquires a concrete image of light rising.
reason: تَرَجَّلَ النهار is the day's rising and spreading light; عَلِيًّا means high or elevated. The senses meet in ascent.

after: Both senses carry a measure of size, but only broadly.
reason: أكبر النهار can mean a larger part of the day, and كَبِيرًا names greatness opposed to smallness. They share scale as a general image.

after: One sense is a rise or protrusion; the other is an unlowered descent into a well. The pair sets upward emergence against downward entry.
reason: تَرَجَّلَ في البئر means descending into a well without being lowered by rope, while نُشُوزَهُنَّ names rising. Their directions oppose each other.

after: The descent into a well pulls against the closing image of divine height. Hearing both makes the coda span the low depth and the exalted height.
reason: تَرَجَّلَ في البئر means going down into a well unaided, while عَلِيًّا means high or exalted. The senses face opposite vertical directions.

after: The calf is left to move with its mother and nurse at will. Beside أَطَعْنَكُمْ, obedience can sound unforced, like freely following an attachment.
reason: إرسال الفصيل مع أمه means letting the young animal stay with its mother and nurse when it wishes; أَطَعْنَكُمْ means willing compliance. Together they picture natural, unforced following.

after: A calf moving beside its mother can travel along a way, but this is a simple movement image.
reason: إرسال الفصيل مع أمه lets the young animal move with its mother, and سَبِيلًا is a path. The route complements their movement only in a broad sense.

after: The horse's stride blends two gaits, while the command names separation. Their movement makes the instruction to break away sound like its opposite.
reason: ارتجال الفرس is mixing the gait with another gait, while وَٱهْجُرُوهُنَّ means to separate or break off. Blending and severance pull in opposite directions.

after: A path is a setting for a horse moving through its mixed gait.
reason: ارتجال الفرس describes a horse mixing two gaits in its run; سَبِيلًا is a route. The route can carry that movement, though the connection is generic.

after: Both senses offer a vertical image, but only by a simple spatial resemblance.
reason: المرجل المنصوب is a cauldron set upright, while عَلِيًّا speaks of being high. Their upright and elevated images meet thinly.

after: An uncharged injury and an expenditure both leave a loss, but the connection is broad.
reason: الرِّجل جبار is harm from an animal's blow for which its rider owes no compensation; أَنفَقُوا۟ describes resources going out as expenditure. The shared image is material loss without recovery.

after: The commanded blow is heard beside a beast's blow whose injury is treated as uncharged. That echo brings agency and liability into the shadow of the command.
reason: الرِّجل جبار is an animal's blow whose damage is not charged to its rider, while وَٱضْرِبُوهُنَّ directly names striking. Both senses meet in the physical blow, though one carries a rule of nonliability.

after: The feared state can be pictured as someone rising and striding into a course of action. This gives نُشُوزَهُنَّ an active, bodily image.
reason: رُكوب الأمر بالرجلين means mounting an undertaking and moving forward, while نُشُوزَهُنَّ names rising-up. Together they picture rising to enter an action.

after: The forbidden seeking becomes a deliberate undertaking entered and pursued. The pair makes the pursuit of a way sound like setting out on foot.
reason: رُكوب الأمر بالرجلين means entering an undertaking and proceeding, while تَبْغُوا۟ means seeking or pursuing. Both senses depict actively going after something.

after: An insect's bite can supply the harm that fear anticipates, though the link is broad.
reason: البعوضة is a biting, harmful mosquito, while تَخَافُونَ is fearing an expected harm. The insect can be the source of the feared harm.

after: The closing word names greatness, while the mosquito's defining image is its tiny body. The contrast in scale lets the verse's greatness be heard against an almost minute creature.
reason: البعوضة is singled out for its small body, while كَبِيرًا means great or large, the opposite of small. Their size senses directly oppose each other.

after: The men's group can be heard as the source of the spending, though this is a broad social link.
reason: أَنفَقُوا۟ means they spent resources, and قَوَّٰمُونَ is glossed here as a group of men. The group supplies the agents of the outflow.

after: The spending ground becomes tangible as wealth leaving its holders. Their assets are the resource from which the outlay departs.
reason: أَنفَقُوا۟ means spending or causing resources to go out, while أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ is their wealth or asset-field. The wealth is the resource spent.

after: The verse names sound women, then the rare branch recalls a false outward show that conceals its opposite. Hearing both sharpens صالحات into integrity measured against hidden contradiction.
reason: النفاق is appearing aligned while concealing an opposite inward stance, whereas فَٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ names sound or good women. False appearance and genuine soundness stand against each other.

after: The unseen is a fitting domain for what hypocrisy conceals. The pairing lets الغَيْب carry the image of an inward truth that outward eyes cannot verify.
reason: النفاق conceals what differs from outward appearance, while الغَيْب is what is hidden from sight or knowledge. Both senses meet in concealment.

after: Hypocrisy keeps an apparent bond while concealing inward departure. Beside هَجْر, it pictures separation masked by an appearance of connection.
reason: النفاق shows one thing while hiding its opposite, and وَٱهْجُرُوهُنَّ means breaking off or separating. Together they make an image of concealed severance.

after: The senses face in opposite directions. In the sequence, separation is set against the possibility of restored concord.
reason: الصُّلْح is reconciliation that removes estrangement, while وَٱهْجُرُوهُنَّ means to separate or break off. Removing disaffection opposes enacting separation.

after: The word for obedience reads as willing alignment with another's direction. Together the senses make compliance a kind of fitting oneself to a relation.
reason: الصلاح للشيء means that something fits or is suitable for you, while أَطَعْنَكُمْ means they align themselves in willing compliance. Both senses speak of fitting or alignment.

after: A fitting thing may be what one seeks, but the connection is general.
reason: الصلاح للشيء is suitability for someone, and تَبْغُوا۟ means seeking or pursuing. A seeker may pursue what fits, a broad complement.

after: The divine giver is also the one toward whom prayerful silence is directed. This rare sense lets devotion shade the ayah's first mention of Allah's ordering.
reason: قَٰنِتَٰتٌ in this branch means holding back from human speech in prayer, and ٱللَّهُ is God, the object of worship. Prayerful silence is one part of worship directed to Him.

after: The Allah who preserves is also the one before whom the devotee holds her tongue. Prayer's silence gives the preservation clause a devotional setting.
reason: The rare sense of قَٰنِتَٰتٌ is abstaining from speech in prayer, while ٱللَّهُ names God as the worshipped. That silence is one mode of worship toward Him.

after: Obedience can be heard as an act of disciplined restraint. The prayer silence makes compliance concrete as holding back one's speech.
reason: قَٰنِتَٰتٌ here means abstaining from human speech in prayer, and أَطَعْنَكُمْ means complying or aligning willingly. Silence is one concrete act of obedience.

after: The prohibition on seeking a way against them is framed before God. Hearing prayerful silence beside His name casts restraint as worshipful discipline.
reason: قَٰنِتَٰتٌ in the rare branch means keeping silent in prayer, while ٱللَّهَ is the one worshipped. The silence is a mode of worship directed toward Him.

after: The pairing offers an image of inwardly retaining what cannot be seen, though only broadly.
reason: حَفِظَتْهُ بمعنى استظهرته is holding something in the mind, while الغَيْب is what is absent from sight or knowledge. The senses meet in an image of preserving what is unseen.
